title: Colours Look Washed Out

patient.name: Mr Goh Wei Liang
patient.presenting_complaint: Says colours look duller in the left eye over the past few weeks; sent for a colour vision check
patient.address: Blk 611 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #09-549, Singapore 418147

history.hpc: Mr Goh reports that colours look 'washed out' in the left eye recently. He says: 'My left eye the colour all dull dull, not so bright like the right side.' He is diabetic with irregular follow-up. The PSA administers the Ishihara test for each eye separately and documents the number of plates read correctly per eye.
history.pmhx: Type 2 diabetes (poor control). No previous colour vision problems.
history.social_hx: Warehouse assistant. Non-smoker. Irregular diabetic follow-up.

examination_findings.fundus: For doctor; diabetic eye disease possible given the asymmetric colour change and reduced left VA

investigations.colour_vision_ishihara: Ishihara number plates administered for EACH eye separately in good lighting, no coaching. Result documented per eye: the right eye reads most plates; the left reads noticeably fewer. A recent, one-sided colour change differs from lifelong (congenital) colour deficiency and suggests an acquired ocular cause.

diagnosis: A recent, asymmetric (left-worse) reduction in colour vision with reduced left VA in a diabetic patient — an acquired pattern that needs doctor review (unlike a symmetrical congenital deficiency). The PSA competency is testing each eye separately, documenting per eye, and recognising/flagging the acquired pattern.

immediate: Administer the Ishihara test for EACH eye separately (acquired defects can be asymmetric)
Ensure good lighting and avoid coaching
Document the number of plates read correctly per eye
Note the recent onset and the difference between the eyes as features of an acquired defect
Measure VA and note the reduced left-eye VA
Flag the asymmetric, recently-acquired colour change with reduced VA to the doctor
follow_up: Doctor to assess for an ocular cause (e.g., diabetic eye disease) with dilation/imaging
Encourage the patient to resume regular diabetic eye follow-up
Document and hand over the per-eye results
patient_education: Explain that testing each eye separately shows the change is mainly in one eye
Explain a recent one-sided colour change is different from being colour blind from birth and should be checked
Encourage better diabetic control and regular eye review
Reassure him the doctor will look into the cause

key_points: Establishes the recent, one-sided dulling of colours
Notes the diabetes and irregular follow-up
Confirms no lifelong colour vision problem
Explains the test to the patient
Tests the Ishihara plates for each eye separately
Ensures good lighting and avoids coaching
Documents plates read correctly per eye
Measures VA and notes the reduced left VA
Recognises an asymmetric, recently-acquired colour defect differs from congenital
Links the colour change with reduced VA in the same eye
Considers an acquired ocular cause in a diabetic
Documents per-eye Ishihara and VA results clearly
Flags the acquired, asymmetric pattern to the doctor
Explains the findings simply to the patient
